# OKR guide

## Good and weak key results

| Weak | Why | Better |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launch the new onboarding flow | A task, not an outcome | Raise 30-day activation from 32% to 45% |
| Improve customer satisfaction | No metric or target | Raise support CSAT from 4.1 to 4.5 out of 5 |
| Get more leads | No baseline or target | Grow qualified leads from 120 to 180 per month |
| Reduce churn a lot | Vague target | Cut monthly logo churn from 3.0% to 2.2% |

## Scoring

- Score = (actual - baseline) / (target - baseline), capped between 0.0 and 1.0.
- Example: baseline 32%, target 45%, actual 41%. Score = (41 - 32) / (45 - 32) = 9 / 13 = 0.69.
- Committed key results should score 1.0. Below that, explain what got in the way.
- Aspirational key results around 0.6 to 0.7 are healthy. Consistent 1.0 scores mean targets were too easy.
- For "reduce" metrics the same formula works because both differences are negative.

## Common mistakes

- Too many objectives. Focus beats coverage.
- Key results nobody can measure with current data.
- Copying last period's OKRs without asking what changed.
- Treating OKRs as a to-do list.
- Using scores to rate individual people.

## Check-in format

| Key result | Owner | Baseline | Target | Current | Confidence (high, medium, low) | Blocker |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
